316134.title: The converse as a conjecture
316134.statement:
For an integer $n\ge 2$, let

$$
\binom{2n-1}{n-1}\equiv 1 \pmod{n^{k}}
$$

denote the congruence between the binomial coefficient
$\binom{2n-1}{n-1}$ and $1$ modulo $n^{k}$, where $k$ is a positive integer.

For every integer $n\ge 2$ such that

$$
\binom{2n-1}{n-1}\equiv 1 \pmod{n^{3}},
$$

the number $n$ is prime. Equivalently, no composite integer $n\ge
2$ satisfies $\binom{2n-1}{n-1}\equiv 1 \pmod{n^{3}}$.
316134.references: 1. Wikipedia, [Wolstenholme's theorem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolstenholme%27s_theorem), the article this problem comes from.

324510.title: Nonexistence conjecture for the half-power-sum congruence in the 1 modulo 4 case
324510.statement:
Let $S_m(n)=\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}j^m$. **Half-power-sum nonexistence conjecture.** For no odd positive integer $n\ge 5$ with $n\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ does

$$
S_{(n-1)/2}(n)\equiv 0\pmod{n^3}
$$

hold. The source proposes this after discussing related congruences and reports computational evidence through $n=20000$; no proof or counterexample is supplied.
324510.source_name: Romeo Meštrović, “A congruence modulo n^3 involving two consecutive sums of powers and its applications”, arXiv:1211.4570 (2012).
324510.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.4570

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of November 2012). “Therefore, any counterexample to Giuga's conjecture must be squarefree.”

383053.title: Do Shannon capacity and its reversible variant coincide?
383053.statement:
[2403.10985](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.10985) introduced the notion of *reversible capacity* of a graph and showed that it is at most the Shannon capacity. It is conjectured there that the two values are equal.

At the finite-length level, it is known to fail: the maximum independent set of $C_7^3$ is strictly larger than the maximum *multirectangular* independent set (corresponding to reversible capacity sets). However, it remains possible that in the large-n limit they converge.
383053.references: A. Meiburg, Bounding the Graph Capacity with Quantum Mechanics and Finite Automata, https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.10985

383772.title: Colin's problems (problem 1)
383772.statement: Let $A$ be a graded algebra over a finite field satisfying Artin's conditions which is birationally PI, i.e. $Q_{\text{gr}}(A)_0$ is PI. Find "weak" conditions $(*)$ so that the deformations (i.e. the lifts to characteristic 0) are also birationally PI.
383772.source_name: AimPL: Noncommutative surfaces and Artin's conjecture (posed by Colin Ingalls)

383811.title: Analogous of paths on iterated monodromy groups for iterated Galois groups of dynamical maps
383811.statement: 1. Can we algebraically construct "nice" paths to describe $G_\infty^{geom}$ by more explicit wreath recursions? More precisely, given $z\in f^{-1}(t)$, can we find explicit endomorphisms of $K_\infty$, perhaps recursively described, sending $t$ to $z$ with nice properties?
383811.source_name: AimPL: Groups of dynamical origin (posed by Ophelia Adams)

383814.title: Orbit equivalence for IMG
383814.statement:
1. Can we find $\varphi \in Homeo(\partial T)$ such that the orbit of the group generated by $\varphi$ and $IMG(f)$ are orbit equivalent? 

2. Can we make $\varphi$ explicit?
383814.source_name: AimPL: Groups of dynamical origin (posed by Constantine Medynets)

383820.title: Maximal subgroups in Thompson groups
383820.statement: Find new maximal subgroups of infinite index in Thompson groups

383823.title: Describe the singularities of the smoothable component of … .
383823.statement:
Describe the singularities of the smoothable component of ${\rm Hilb}^d(\mathbb{A}^n)$. To be more specific:

How large can the dimension of the Zariski tangent space to this component get?

Does the maximum occur in the intersection of components? Does it occur in the smoothable component?

383825.title: Hilbert schemes of points (problem 3)
383825.statement: What is the smallest $d$ such that ${\rm Hilb}^d(\mathbb{A}^3)$ is reducible?

383835.title: What can we say about the set … ?
383835.statement: What can we say about the set $Z^e$? Can we construct exotic components (i.e. components that only exist in characteristic $p$) using this stratification? Study the action by the Galois group ${\rm Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p/\mathbb{F}_p)$.

383839.title: Hilbert schemes of curves (problem 5)
383839.statement: Fix $d,g,n$. Find a good/sharp lower bound for the dimension of components of ${\rm Hilb}_{d,g}(\mathbb{P}^n)$.

383841.title: What is the largest number of points in general position you can make these curves pass through?
383841.statement: What is the largest number of points in general position you can make these curves pass through?

383855.title: The $u$-invariant problem (problem 2)
383855.statement:
Find interesting classes $\mathcal F$ of fields such that for $F \in
 \mathcal F$,

$$
u(F) < \infty \Longrightarrow u(F(t)) < \infty.
$$
383855.source_name: AimPL: Deformation theory and the Brauer group

383857.title: The $u$-invariant problem (problem 4)
383857.source_name: AimPL: Deformation theory and the Brauer group

383870.title: Characteristic $p>0$ invariants (problem 8)
383870.statement: Fix $d$. What is the maximum value of the $F$-pure threshold of $\mathfrak{m}$ of a non-${\\mathbb{Q}}$-Gorenstein local ring $(R, \mathfrak{m})$ of dimension $d$?
383870.source_name: AimPL: Test ideals and multiplier ideals (posed by Watanabe)

384643.title: Toeplitz Determinants and Toeplitz Operators (problem 4)
384643.statement: (Berger-Coburr 1994): On the Fock/Bergman space, define the projection $\prod:L^2(\mathbb{C},e^{-|z|^2}dA) \rightarrow \mathscr{F}_{\mathbb{C}}$. Take $p: \mathbb{C} \rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ and define $T_p(f)=\prod(p(z)f(z))$. $T_p$ is bounded on the Fock space iff for all $(x,y) \in \mathbb{R}^2$, $u_t=\Delta u,$ $u\Big|_{t=0}=p$, and $u(\frac{1}{4},x,y)$ are bounded.
384643.source_name: AimPL: Riemann-Hilbert problems, Toeplitz matrices, and applications (posed by Michael Hitrik)

387647.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 4.14
387647.statement: Does there exist a polynomial of the type in Problem 4.13, for which $$ \min_{|z|=1}|P(z)|>C_2\sqrt{n} $$ for every $n$? More generally, does there exist such a polynomial satisfying both ([source label: 4.1]) and ([source label: 4.2])?
387647.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

388918.title: Scalar Curvature Question [?55]: 18
388918.statement: Conjecture 18. Interior Hemi-Spherical Area Inequality. The r-interiors of all compact Riemanninn-manifolds X with boundaries and withSc(X) ≥Sc(Sn) =n(n−1) satisfy for all r ≥π/2, co-s+ar(X−r) ≤2π∶ no strictly area decreasing proper mapX−r→Sn + of non-zero degree for r > π/2 exists. It is even unclear what happens in this regard to domains in closed spin manifoldsX. For instance:
388918.source_name: Gromov - 101 Questions, Problems and Conjectures around Scalar Curvature (2017) (proposed by Misha Gromov)

390133.title: Conjecture — For every finitely generated subgroups G of ModS, the group Φf (G) is nilpotent.
390133.statement: For every finitely generated subgroups G of ModS, the group Φf (G) is nilpotent. For a a little bit more detailed discussion, see [ I4], Section 10.10. I repeated here this old problem in order to stress that our understanding of the subgroups of finite index in Mod S is rather limited.
390133.source_name: Farb - Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics

395340.title: A Ramanujan-type supercongruence labeled (0.4)
395340.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2008/45](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/2091), page 36. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

396518.title: No M-factor in the A-polynomial of 2-bridge knots
396518.statement: For every 2-bridge knot $K$, the A-polynomial of $K$ has no factor depending only on $M$; that is, Conjecture 0.44 holds for all 2-bridge knots.
396518.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2010/35](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4416), page 45. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

396841.title: Alon's 100-dominating directed graph problem
396841.statement: Call a directed graph $D=(V,E)$ $s$-dominating if, for any subset $U$ of at most $s$ vertices of $V$, there is a vertex $v$ such that $(v,u)$ is a directed edge for every $u\in U$. Is it true that any 100-dominating finite directed graph contains a directed cycle of length at most 100?
396841.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/01](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4791), page 70. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

397420.title: Seymour’s 1-flowing conjecture
397420.statement: The 1-flowing conjecture predicts that the max-flow min-cut relation holds for all binary matroids that have no minor in $S := \{AG(3,2),T_{11},T_{11}^{*}\}$.
397420.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/53](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11451), page 28. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

398517.title: Conjectural structure of the unstable \[mathbb A^1\]-homotopy sheaf of a punctured affine space
398517.statement:
Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic different from $2$. For every integer $n\ge 4$, there is an exact sequence of sheaves
\[
K^M_{n+2}/24\longrightarrow \pi^{\mathbb A^1}_n(\mathbb A^n\setminus 0)\longrightarrow GW^{n}_{n+1}.
\]
The sequence becomes short exact after $n$-fold contraction.
398517.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/32](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12495), page 32. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

398672.title: Improve the one-dimensional uniform-distribution discrepancy constant
398672.statement: Let $c^*$ be the supremum of the constants $c$ such that, for every sequence $(x_n)_{n\ge 0}$ in $[0,1)$, the discrepancy satisfies $D_N \ge c\,\frac{\log N}{N}$ for infinitely many $N$. The report gives $0.06458\ldots \le c^* \le 0.222\ldots$. **Open Problem 2:** Improve this estimate for $c^*$, for example by the method indicated in the talk.
398672.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/49](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12723), page 35. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

398683.title: Serre’s uniformity problem for rational points on prime-level modular curves
398683.statement: For every prime $p>37$, the rational points on each of the modular curves $X_0(p)$, $X_s^+(p)$, and $X_{\mathrm{ns}}^+(p)$ consist only of the cusps and the CM-points. Here the CM-points are the rational points arising from elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ with complex multiplication, according as $p$ is ramified, split, or inert in the relevant endomorphism order.
398683.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/51](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12725), page 7. Canonicalized from 5 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

398684.title: Serre’s uniformity problem for the nonsplit Cartan modular curve
398684.statement: For every prime number $p>37$, the rational points on the modular curve $X^+_{\mathrm{ns}}(p)$ consist only of the cusps and the CM-points.
398684.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/51](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12725), page 8. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

399774.title: Entropy minimization problem for incompressible viscous fluids
399774.statement:
Let $X=\mathbb{T}^n$ and $\Omega=C([0,1],X)$. Let $R$ be the reversible Brownian path measure on $X$ with initial marginal $R_0=\mathrm{vol}$ and generator $\Delta/2$. Given a coupling $\pi\in\mathcal{P}(X^2)$ with $\pi_0=\pi_1=\mathrm{vol}$, minimize
\[
H(P\mid R)\quad\text{over }P\in\mathcal{P}(\Omega)\text{ such that }P_t=\mathrm{vol}\ \text{for all }0\le t\le1,\quad P_{01}=\pi.
\]
399774.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2015/35](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/13856), page 18. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

399987.title: Exact satisfiability threshold for random 4-SAT
399987.statement: Conjecturally, the exact satisfiability threshold for random $4$-SAT is $m=9.93\ldots n$, where $n$ is the number of variables and $m$ is the number of independent uniformly random constraints.
399987.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2015/54](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/13949), page 25. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

401029.title: Finiteness of level-1 algebraic cuspidal automorphic representations of bounded motivic weight
401029.statement: For every integer $N\ge 1$, there are only finitely many cuspidal automorphic representations $\pi$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, with $n$ varying, whose Artin conductor is $N$ and which are algebraic of motivic weight $\le 23$.
401029.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2017/25](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/15433), page 14. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

402016.title: Coloring count cones for plane near-triangulations with a 5-cycle outer face
402016.statement: For every plane near-triangulation $G$ with the outer face bounded by a 5-cycle, $n_G^\star$ is a non-negative linear combination of $n_{G_1},\ldots,n_{G_{11}}$.
402016.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2019/1](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/16763), page 20. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

402456.title: Asymptotic count of $E_2$ almost primes in short intervals
402456.statement:
Let $E_2$ denote the set of integers of the form $p_1p_2$, where $p_1,p_2$ are primes. For every fixed $\theta>0.55$, for sufficiently large $x$ and $H\\ge x^\theta$, one has
\[
\sum_{\substack{x<n\le x+H\\ n\in E_2}}1
=H\frac{\log\log x}{\log x}+O\!\left(H\frac{\log\log\log x}{\log x}\right).
\]
402456.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2019/50](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/17293), page 38. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

402824.title: Banach’s geometric hypothesis in the exceptional case $n=133$
402824.statement: Does every finite-dimensional real Banach space $V$ whose $133$-dimensional subspaces are all mutually isometric necessarily have an ellipsoidal unit ball, and hence be a Hilbert space? Equivalently, if all $133$-dimensional sections of the unit ball are affinely equivalent, must the unit ball be an ellipsoid?
402824.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2020/30](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1703876), page 26. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

403149.title: Bounded $H^\infty$-calculus for the degenerate boundary realization
403149.statement: Under the setup on page 41, let $A_T$ be the $L^p$-realization of $A$ with boundary condition $T$. For every $0<\theta<\pi$, there exists a constant $\nu$ such that $A_T+\nu$ has a bounded $H^\infty$-calculus in $L^p(X)$.
403149.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2021/27](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/7155448), page 41. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

403537.title: Stabilization of the dimension of Teichmüller modular forms
403537.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2021/6](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4990375), page 21. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

405048.title: Super-exponential anticoncentration for the permanent of a random Bernoulli matrix
405048.statement: Can the exponential upper bound in Theorem 1 be improved to a super-exponential bound? More specifically, for a uniformly random $n\times n$ matrix $A_n$ with entries in $\{-1,1\}$, can the bound $\Pr[\operatorname{per}(A_n)=x]\le \exp(-cn)$, for every $x\in\mathbb R$ and some absolute constant $c>0$, be strengthened to a super-exponential bound, as conjectured by Vu [20, Conjecture 6.12]?
405048.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2026/1](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14299905), page 18. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

405055.title: Lower bound relating the window parameter to positional variance
405055.statement: **Conjecture 10.** For every finite poset $P$ of size $n$ and every element $x\in P$, $\operatorname{win}(x)=\Omega\!\left(\frac{\sigma^2(x)}{n}\right)$, where $\sigma^2(x)=\operatorname{Var}(f(x))$.
405055.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2026/1](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14299905), page 34. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

405708.title: London’s conjecture
405708.statement: For every prime power $q$ such that $q\notin\{7,9,11,13\}$, let $n=q^{2}+q+1$. Among all $C_{4}$-free graphs $G$ on $n$ vertices with $\lvert E(G)\rvert=\frac{1}{2}q(q+1)^{2}$, one has $\tau(G)\le n^{(n-3)/2}$, with equality if and only if $G$ is an orthogonal polarity graph.
405708.references: - [A Turán-type extremal problem for the number of spanning trees in C4-free graphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34616) — arXiv — Shaohan Xu, Fengming Dong, Kexiang Xu

406041.title: Green problem 45
406041.statement: Can we pick residue classes $a_p \pmod{p}$, one for each prime $p \leq N$, such that every integer $\leq N$ lies in at least $10$ of them? Erdős remarks that he does not know how to answer it with $10$ replaced by $2$; this is `Erdos689.erdos_689`.

406147.title: OEIS A185150 conjecture
406147.statement:
Let $a(n)$ denote [OEIS A185150](https://oeis.org/A185150), with its indexing and defining sequence as given there.

Conjecture: $a(n) > 0$ for all $n > 0$. - _Zhi-Wei Sun_, Dec 29 2012
